decisions.reason: The battery-efficiency goal adds a power-management constraint but does not change the single-board architecture, functional consolidation, or functionality-preservation requirements.

Battery efficiency is an independent power-management goal; the source does not cancel or alter the integrated board's cost, component-tier, connector-reduction, or functionality-preservation constraints.
The general battery-efficiency goal does not specify any change to the existing main-board OR-ing method, sources, or source-selection behavior.
The source does not change the DCDC1 voltage setpoint, configuration interface, downstream rail target, or diode-drop compensation.
Efficient battery use does not necessarily change the legacy main-board connector inventory or connector architecture.
The battery-efficiency objective has no entailed effect on the LED board's power-and-data pin ordering.
Although current monitoring may help evaluate efficiency, the source does not change the monitor IC, monitored rails, channel allocation, or measurement placement.
The efficiency goal does not resolve or alter the battery connector's pinout, placement, orientation, family, or mounting style.
Maximizing operating time does not entail a change to the existing battery-protection modes or cutoff settings.
The source does not change the requirement to monitor battery temperature through the J_BAT NTC connection.
The battery-efficiency goal does not alter how charge status is indicated or any associated connector, resistor, or population settings.
The source establishes an electrical efficiency objective but does not necessarily change the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting, connector placement, or enclosure-fit constraints.
